_doc: The words of the Ledger (scripts/sim/advisor.gd builds the card from them; scripts/ui/ledger_card.gd draws it). The Ledger is the guidance program Ma Gantry Loans installs on every ship it finances (docs/LORE.md): dry, polite, financial, faintly threatening and sometimes accidentally kind, and it says one short line at a time. stages: the checklist of each stage in order (the milestone ladder of docs/audit/progression.md section 7): id, title, why and check. A check is {key: number} (every key must be met; a number is a literal or "p:<key>", read from that stage's row of data/progression.json) or a list of such objects (any one will do); a key is one of advisor.gd VOCAB, met at or above its number (damaged_blocks: at or below). A clause whose p: number is missing is left out, a goal with nothing left is dropped (so the stage 1 and 2 goals work before the balance track's file lands). {=key} in a title or why is filled with that check's number. {id} or {id:words} marks a mechanic keyword (keywords below: a colour and a hover line). tips: the first-time notes, one per profile each, listed in the journal (advisor.gd TIPS says what each waits for). warnings: one line each (advisor.gd WARNINGS); each fires at most once a stage unless it gets worse by rules.worse. rules: worse = how much worse (x) a warning must get to fire again in the same stage; toll_jumps, toll_scrap: the toll warning's range and scrap; scrap_credits: the unspent scrap warning's credits; hull_stations: jumps to the next station for the hull warning; warn_s: seconds a warning stays on the card; pace_s: seconds between two looks (at least 1); low_fuel: the fuel of the low fuel tip. labels: how a check is named in the progress (Guns 2/3). keywords: the colours differ from each other and from describe.json's (tests/test_advisor.gd measures it).

card.title: THE LEDGER
card.done: Everything on the list is done. Ma has nothing to add, which is rare.

intake.hover: Pulls in debris that touches it. Mount it on an outer wall.

gun.hover: Weapons that need power and a hull mount or a room.

shield.hover: Layers that absorb hits before the hull.

fabricator.hover: Builds parts from blueprints. Modules raise its level.

blueprint.hover: A recipe you can craft. Found, scanned or bought.

fuel.hover: One jump burns one. Stations and canisters supply it.

toll.hover: What the warden charges to open the exit lane.

warden.hover: Holds the exit lane of each region.

armour.hover: Solid tiles that soak hits. Cheap, and they need no power.

engine.hover: Thrust against mass. More guns need more engines.

ion.hover: Knocks shields out and stuns crew.

1.title: Mount your {intake}.
1.why: A third of your scrap drifts past. The net mouth is in the hold, earning nothing, like a cousin.

1.title: Fit three {gun:guns}.
1.why: Your collateral would like a third gun.

1.title: Add a {shield} or a {medbay}.
1.why: Ma would like the collateral to survive its first fight. One layer or one bed will do.

1.title: Hold enough {fuel} for the road to the beacon.
1.why: A stranded ship repays nobody. Ma has checked.

1.title: Keep the {warden}'s {toll} in your pocket.
1.why: The exit lane is not free, and the warden does not take scrap. Ma recommends solvency.

2.title: Upgrade the {fabricator}.
2.why: A Robot Arm in its room makes level two, which builds what the shops are too proud to sell.

2.title: Arm to {=guns} guns and {=layers} layers.
2.why: The collateral is growing. Ma finds this encouraging, in writing.

2.title: Add {engine:engines} as you add guns.
2.why: Every gun is mass, and slow ships get repossessed.

2.title: Look for better parts: {=known} {blueprint:blueprints}.
2.why: Take every Scan row. Mk2 recipes turn up in shops, wrecks and aboard stations.

2.title: Fatten the purse before the beacon.
2.why: The {warden} wants its {toll} and a little goodwill. Sell surplus scrap at a station.

3.title: Brace: {=guns} guns behind {=layers} layers.
3.why: Tier-three enemies start about now. They have not read your file.

3.title: Mount a second {intake}.
3.why: More mouths, more scrap. The drift does not mind being collected.

3.title: Raise the {fabricator} to level {=fab}.
3.why: An Assembly Rig and two Robot Arms. The titanium loop starts here.

3.title: Add {=plates} {armour:plates}.
3.why: Armour is cheaper than an apology.

3.title: Credits for the {toll}.
3.why: Sell scrap before the beacon. The warden has seen your balance and has opinions.

4.title: Field {=guns} guns behind {=layers} layers.
4.why: Every enemy carries a shield now. {ion} and {missile:missiles} go through; the shops know.

4.title: Keep your speed above {=accel_ratio}.
4.why: A barge loses the intake and the aim. Add {engine:engines}.

4.title: Plate up to {=plates}.
4.why: Ma notes that hulls are the only collateral that fights back.

4.title: Know {=known} {blueprint:blueprints}.
4.why: Mk2 and Mk3 parts are on the shelves. The Ledger can only suggest; the purse decides.

4.title: Credits for the {toll}.
4.why: The lane costs more each stage. So does everything Ma sells.

5.title: Field {=guns} guns behind {=layers} layers.
5.why: The listening posts hear everything, including your shield count.

5.title: Raise the {fabricator} to level {=fab}.
5.why: Higher levels build the parts that make the rest of the ship look cheap.

5.title: Plate up to {=plates}.
5.why: Armour does not need a reactor, which the Ledger finds restful.

5.title: Know {=known} {blueprint:blueprints}.
5.why: Read the stores, take the Scan rows, board what you can.

5.title: Credits for the {toll}.
5.why: A good ship pays at the beacon and never has to be kind about it.

6.title: Field {=guns} guns behind {=layers} layers.
6.why: The doors are open, and so are the enemy's. Ma recommends being larger.

6.title: Keep the lights on.
6.why: Every gun draws power, and a ship in the red does not shoot. Ma does the sums.

6.title: Plate up to {=plates}.
6.why: Every plate is a sentence the enemy has to finish.

6.title: Mend the damage before the beacon.
6.why: Stations repair every block. The warden does not.

6.title: Credits for the {toll}.
6.why: Sell the surplus scrap at a station and the rest is arithmetic.

7.title: Field {=guns} guns behind {=layers} layers.
7.why: The enemy has stopped being polite. Ma suggests you stop being small.

7.title: Plate up to {=plates}.
7.why: The heavier the ship, the longer the debt can be discussed.

7.title: Mend the damage before the beacon.
7.why: A dented ship is only a ship that has not paid yet.

7.title: Credits for the {toll}.
7.why: Ma has been told the lane is expensive. She finds this relatable.

8.title: Field {=guns} guns behind {=layers} layers.
8.why: The last stage. Ma would like the collateral to finish what it started.

8.title: Plate up to {=plates}.
8.why: The last stage hits like the first, from further away.

8.title: Mend the damage before the beacon.
8.why: The Ledger would like the collateral intact at the end. It would like many things.

8.title: Credits for the {toll}.
8.why: One last lane. Ma will want to hear about it.

tips.title: Build mode
tips.text: The world holds still while you build. Cable every part to a reactor, then press B to fly.

tips.title: Your first fight
tips.text: Shields first, then guns, then hull: the hull is the collateral. J jumps away when the odds look rude.

tips.title: A breach
tips.text: A room is losing air. Repair seals it, Evacuate abandons it. Ma values the crew above the carpet.

tips.title: A station
tips.text: Docked. Stations repair every block, sell fuel and parts, and buy scrap. Sell the surplus before the beacon.

tips.title: The fabricator
tips.text: It builds what you hold a blueprint for. A higher level opens more recipes: add a Robot Arm to its room.

tips.title: A blueprint
tips.text: Yours for good. Craft the part at the fabricator (C), then place it from the palette (B).

tips.title: Shields
tips.text: Layers can be moved between the sectors of the bubble. Put the thick side toward whoever is shooting.

tips.title: A warden
tips.text: It holds the exit lane. Pay the toll, break through or turn back. Ma suggests whichever leaves you solvent.

tips.title: A drift jump
tips.text: It burns no fuel and costs hull instead. Ma will not be reimbursing the hull.

tips.title: Low fuel
tips.text: Stations sell it, and debris sometimes carries canisters. A stranded ship pays nobody.

tips.title: Boarding
tips.text: Choose who goes aboard and what they carry. Mods in the kit slot change how the boarding goes.

tips.title: A mod
tips.text: A small device worn in a kit slot. Fit it on the loadout screen before the next boarding.

tips.title: The Salvage Rig
tips.text: It added to what you opened. Higher marks add more. Ma has noted the percentage.

tips.title: A new crewmate
tips.text: Select them, then click a button on the crew bar: they are posted to that station for good.

tips.title: A wrecked part
tips.text: It stays wrecked. Repair at a station, and keep spares in the hold.

outgunned.text: The warden outguns you and the lane is out of reach. Ma recommends not dying; it complicates repayment.

fuel.text: Fuel will not reach the beacon. A stranded ship repays nobody, and Ma has checked.

skulls.text: That contact outguns you. Ma suggests leaving; she values your continued interest.

toll.text: The toll is near and the purse is thin. Sell scrap at a station: Ma's cousin buys everything.

hull.text: The structure is thin and the next station is far. Mend it before the collateral becomes a rumour.

cliff.text: The next region outguns you. Ma recommends not dying; it complicates repayment.

power.text: Demand exceeds supply, and parts go dark. Add a reactor, or take a gun off the books.

mass.text: The ship is heavy and slow, and slow ships get caught. Add engines.

scrap.text: Scrap in the hold, arrears on the account. Sell the surplus at a station; Ma prefers coin.

blueprints.text: No new blueprints in a long while. Take the Scan rows and read the stores; progress is a recurring cost.
